Surat al-Bayyina

It is also called Surat al-Qayyima, Surat al-Munfakkin, and Surat al-Bariyya. Its number of verses is eight, and it is Medinan according to the most sound opinion.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: 'God has commanded me to recite to you: ﴿Those who disbelieved were not [going to desist]...﴾.' He said: 'And He named me to you?' He said: 'Yes.' So he wept." It was also narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

In another narration of Imam Ahmad, from Abu Habba al-Badri, he said: "When ﴿Those who disbelieved were not [going to desist]﴾ was revealed, Jibril said: 'O Messenger of God! Your Lord commands you to recite it to Ubayy.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ubayy: 'Jibril has commanded me to recite this surah to you.' Ubayy said: 'And I was mentioned there, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then Ubayy wept.'"

(p-6225) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discourse on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[1–3] ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist until there came to them clear evidence﴾ ﴿a messenger from God, reciting purified pages﴾ [al-Bayyina: 2] ﴿within which are upright scriptures﴾ [al-Bayyina: 3]

﴿Those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., those who denied the prophethood of the Prophet, God's blessings be upon him, out of their obstinacy after they had clearly discerned the truth in it. ﴿Among the People of the Book﴾, i.e., the Jews and Christians who knew him, heard his proofs, and witnessed his signs, ﴿and the polytheists﴾, i.e., the idolaters of the Arabs. ﴿Were not going to desist﴾, i.e., from their heedlessness and ignorance of the truth, and their adherence to what they had inherited from their forefathers, knowing nothing of the truth. ﴿Until there came to them clear evidence﴾, i.e., the decisive proof that establishes the claim, and here it is the Prophet (ﷺ). His coming is what stirred up what had become firmly rooted in their beliefs and entrenched in their customs, so that they began to argue in their obstinacy and contentiousness that he was something already known to them, whom they could reach through what they already possessed; but he does not deserve to be followed, for what they are upon is more beautiful and more original, and following the forefathers in it is more appealing and more pleasing to souls. That clear evidence which makes them recognize the face of truth is: ﴿a messenger from God﴾ [al-Bayyina: 2], i.e., Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿reciting purified pages﴾ [al-Bayyina: 2], which are the pages of the Qur'an, purified from confusion and the interpolations of distorters; therefore rays of truth radiate from them, so that both its seekers and its deniers recognize it together.

﴿Within which are upright scriptures﴾ [al-Bayyina: 3], i.e., straight, with no crookedness in them. The uprightness of scriptures is their containing the truth that does not incline toward falsehood: ﴿Falsehood does not approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42]. As for the scriptures that are in the pages and copies of the Qur'an, they are either those of the earlier books that are sound, such as those of Moses, Jesus, and others, which God related from them in His Book, for He has not brought from them except what is strong and sound. He has left aside the narration of what the distorters have obscured, unless its mention is to explain its falsity; for this reason, those who denied his messengership, peace be upon him, from the People of the Book found no way to deny the truth, and they only preferred other than it, saying that the Qur'an's surahs are [merely] scriptures; for every surah of his is an upright scripture. So the pages of the Qur'an and the leaves of its codex, containing surahs of the Qur'an, are upright scriptures. Since a questioner might ask: if these who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists have disengaged from that all-enveloping darkness, and the truth has appeared to them such that they recognize it as they recognize their own sons, then why did they not believe in this truth that came to them? The Truth, Exalted is He, answered that the People of the Book had been given clear evidence and decisive proof of the truth whose face does not differ, through what God revealed to their prophets; and it was incumbent upon them to seek guidance from their books in knowing His path so that they would not deviate from it. When a doubt arose for one of them, he was to return for its resolution to one knowledgeable in the meanings of the books. Then it was incumbent upon them to strive to learn their meanings, understand their methods, and preserve them, so that no misleader would misguide them concerning them. But this clear evidence did not benefit them at all, for they differed in interpretation and split into sects, until the people of each sect nullified what the people of the other sect held. That was out of their transgression, persistence in their aims, and insistence upon what their desire had led them to. This is His, the Exalted's, saying:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 98, verses 4–5:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[4–5] ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after there had come to them clear evidence﴾ ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, inclining toward truth (hunafa'), and to establish prayer and give zakah. And that is the upright religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5]

﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after there had come to them clear evidence﴾ means: through the tongues of their prophets (p-6227). Thus was their conduct regarding the Prophet (ﷺ): they denied his clear evidence just as they denied the clear evidence of their prophets, by dividing over it and by straying from its reality through division. If this was the condition of the People of the Scripture regarding their clear evidence and ours, then what do you think of the polytheists, who are more deeply rooted in ignorance and more easily led by desire than they are? And His words, Exalted is He, ﴿And they were not commanded﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5] mean: while the People of the Scripture were not commanded through the language of their prophets and their books ﴿except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5], that is, submission and humility. This is achieved by purifying it from having anything associated with Him in it: no intermediary, no wealth, no honor, and no status. ﴿Hunafa'﴾ means: followers of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), or those who are upon his way. Its root is the plural of (hanif), meaning one who inclines away and turns aside. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was named with it because he turned away from the idolatry of all the people. ﴿And establish prayer﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5] means: performing it, so that the heart is present, reverent before the One worshipped, and trained by humility, not merely being outward movements, for that is not prayer at all. ﴿And give zakah﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5] means: spending it in the channels that Allah, Exalted is He, has specified.

﴿And that is the upright religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5] means: the upright books, or the religion of the upright, straight community. The meaning of the verse is that the People of the Scripture divided, and each sect cursed the other. Their division was in beliefs, rulings, and the branches of the Sharia, even though they were not commanded, and those rulings were not established for them, except so that they would worship Allah and make their beliefs and their deeds sincerely for Him. Thus they should not take them except from Him directly, and not imitate the people of misguidance among the other nations, and that they should humble themselves before Allah in their prayer, and that they should join the servants of Allah through their zakah. If this is the principle to which the commands are referred, then it was incumbent upon them to place it before their eyes, referring to it every issue that arises for them, and resolving with it every problem that confronts them. When sincerity governs the souls, fairness dominates them, the unity prevails among them, and division does not find its paths. This is what Allah has denounced concerning the condition of the People of the Scripture. So what shall we say about our condition? Does not our Book, which testifies against us for the evil of our deeds, denounce our division in religion, and that we have become sects in it, and have filled it with innovations and heresies? By what has preceded, you have come to know that those who disbelieved are those who denied the messengership of the Prophet (ﷺ) when they were called to accept what he brought. And "min" in His words "min Ahl al-Kitab" [among the People of the Scripture] is for partitive (tab'id, indicating a part of a whole). As for the meaning of "lam yakunu munfakkin" [they were not separating]:

(p-6228) That is: the face of truth had not been about to be revealed to them, so that the earthquake would occur in their beliefs, and they would separate from the pure heedlessness in which they were, until the clear evidence came to them. It is also permissible that what is meant by "those who disbelieved," and Allah knows best, are those who denied some part of the religion of Allah, Exalted is He, when it came to them, and did not consider its proof, or turned away from it after they knew its proof, whether they were among the polytheists of the Arabs or among the People of the Scripture, even if they believed afterward and affirmed. So Allah wished to mention His favor upon those of them who believed. He clarified that those who disbelieved, that is, those who denied what Allah had obligated His servants to believe about His attributes and laws, from among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists of the Arabs, were not going to turn back from their disbelief and denial until the Messenger came to them, clarifying for them the falsehood of what they were upon of disbelief, so that they would believe. How great is the grace of Allah upon them in sending His Messenger to them! This is a different aspect from the one we presented regarding the meaning of "those who disbelieved" and their separation. By this, or by this, the meaning of "hatta" [until] became clear, and all that many commentators babble, whom imitation has led astray from sound opinion, was invalidated. They made the easy parts of the Qur'an difficult, and forbade its people from understanding it. The words of the Imam have ended. We have transmitted them verbatim from the beginning of the surah to here, for their excellence, and because it is the best by which it has been explained. Our principle, which we have followed in this tafsir, is to prefer in the meanings of its verses the best of what has been said about them. Therefore we named it (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) [The Beauties of Interpretation]. May Allah guide us to the most upright path.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[6] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally. They are the worst of creation.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾ means: in God and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so they denied his prophethood. ﴿among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally. They are the worst of creation﴾ means: the worst of those whom God created and brought into being. The Imam said: "Because one who rejects the truth, after knowing it and after the proof has been established against him, is in reality one who has harmed his own intellect, ruined his own soul, and brought ruin upon others."

**Subtleties (lata'if):**

The first: this verse and the one before it show that the designation "the polytheists" (al-mushrikin), in the usage of the Qur'an, does not include the People of the Scripture. Rather, it is specific to the idolaters, meaning those who adhere to associating partners with God and multiplying gods. The People of the Scripture, namely the Jews and the Christians, are not covered by this designation, even though association (shirk) has entered their beliefs, because it is an intruder and not an original part of their faith. For this reason they recoil from the stigma of polytheism, and because of this, marriage with them is permitted, unlike with the idolaters.

The second: Ibn Jarir said: "The Arabs do not hamz (pronounce the glottal stop in) al-bariyyah (البريَّة)." The readers of the major regional cities (qurra' al-amsar) recited it without hamza, with the exception of something mentioned from Nafi' ibn Abi Na'im, for some transmitters reported from him that he did pronounce the hamza, and he took it as derived from God's saying, ﴿before We bring it into being﴾ [al-Hadid: 22], and that it is of the form fa'iyah (فعيلة) from that root. As for those who did not pronounce the hamza, their omission of it has two possible explanations. One is that they omitted the hamza in it just as they omitted it in al-malak (المَلَك), which is of the form mafal (مَفْعَل), from (alaka) or (la'aka), and in (yara), (tara) and (nara), which are of the form tafal (تَفْعَل) from ra'aytu. The other is that they understood it as fa'aliyyah (فَعَلِيَّة), from al-bara' (البَراء), which means dust. It is transmitted from the Arabs by oral report that they say: "bifika al-barrad" (بِفِيكَ البَرّادُ), meaning by it the dust. End.

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[7–8] ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds are the best of creation.﴾ ﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence (ʿAdn), beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 8]

﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾ means: in God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God's blessings be upon him. ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ means: from giving one's self in striving in the way of jihad for the truth, and giving one's wealth in acts of righteousness, along with upholding the obligatory acts of worship and sincerity in all kinds of dealings. This is because their sound submission (idhʿan) and their feeling the pleasure of knowing the truth made the truth take command of them, so they performed righteous deeds. So said the Imam. ﴿They are the best of (p-6230) creation﴾ means: the most excellent of creatures, because by following the truth upon knowing it through the evidence that establishes it, they have realized for themselves the meaning of humanity (insaniyyah) with which God has honored them. And through righteous action, they have preserved the system of virtue, which God made the foundation of human existence, and they have guided others by good example to the same good and happiness to which they themselves were guided. Who, then, could be better than them? So said the Imam.

﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence (ʿAdn), beneath which rivers flow﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 8] means: gardens of lasting abode, with no departure from them, and rivers flowing beneath their trees and mansions. ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 8] means: remaining continuously, never leaving them and never dying in them. ﴿God is pleased with them﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 8] means: because they obeyed Him in this world and acted to be freed from His punishment, this is that (reward). ﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 8] because, through the goodness of their certainty, they find comfort in complying with what He commands in this world, so they are content with Him. Then, when they attain the blessings of the Hereafter, they find of God's grace what leaves no room for resentment, so they are content with God in every state. So said the Imam.

﴿That﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 8] means: this good reward and this pleasure. ﴿For whoever fears his Lord﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 8] means: whoever feared God in this world, inwardly and outwardly, and so guarded himself against Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, for fear of God (khashyah) is the foundation of true happiness.

The Imam said: By this lofty statement he intended to take precaution against the misunderstanding into which common people fall, and continue to fall, and even the elite as well. It is that mere belief by inheritance and imitation of one's parents, knowledge of the outward forms of some rulings, and performance of some acts of worship such as the movements of prayer and abstaining from fasting, these alone are not sufficient to attain what God has prepared as reward for those who believe and do righteous deeds, even if their hearts are filled with envy, rancor, arrogance and ostentation, their mouths are full of lying, slander and calumny, the winds of vanity and conceit sway their sides, their inner selves are a dwelling for servitude and subjugation to rulers, and even to those below rulers, and are empty of the least degree of humility and sincerity toward the Lord of the earth and the heavens. No, they do not attain the goodness of the reward, for the fear of their Lord has not settled in their hearts, and therefore it has not refined their souls. That reward is only for whoever fears his Lord and whose fear has made his heart feel it. And God knows best.
